d4d_fields.description: The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging, waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for external validation of models.

d4d_fields.source_caveats: The two sources that quantify the dataset disagree. The tier-2 project documentation (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that "As of August 2025, covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions" and that 1000 images are currently available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+, Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the dataset content.
